transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortega, Marcus Chen, Aditi Rao, Samir Patel (Redwood); Priya Shah, Evan Brooks, Marta Ruiz, Jon Park (Helios)

Summary: quick hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming behavior, key params (temperature, top_p, max tokens), retry/backoff patterns, observability in the Console and Optimize suggestions around batching/caching. Customer interested in low-latency checkout assistant for commerce site; raised questions about data residency, KMS, SOC2, and fallback to cheaper models under load.

Topics: Hosted streaming, param tuning, retries/backoff, idempotency, console tracing, Optimize recommendations, POC next steps

00:00 Lena: ok, thanks so much everyone for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, i'm the AE, this should be a fairly focused 30–45 minute session demoing our hosted chat endpoint and going through best practices for streaming and retrying, uh, so Marcus and Aditi will drive the technical bits.
00:15 Priya: hi thanks, i'm Priya, CTO at Helios, Evan and Jon are on the call to cover infra, and Marta for product. our main goal is a real-time checkout assistant on web, target p95 under 300ms, and we need to understand cost trade-offs.
00:30 Marcus: great, that's helpful. quick show of hands, are you already calling streaming endpoints today or is everything synchronous?
00:40 Evan: currently sync via hosted third parties, so we get whole response back, it's often 700–1k ms, and that spikes on Black Friday.
00:52 Marcus: ok, so streaming can give perceived latency improvements by returning tokens as they're generated; we also have continuous batching under the hood to balance throughput/cost.
01:05 Aditi: i'll share my screen, start in the Console — here's a running streaming request, you can see partial chunks arrive, and the client shows incremental UI updates. sometimes the transcript notes we get small jitter when the model fetches KV cache entries, we've seen that called "CV cache" in some transcripts before, sorry, that was a typo in earlier notes.
01:30 Marta: that incremental display is key for UX; if the first token shows quickly, even with longer tail, conversion rates improve.
01:42 Marcus: exactly. for parameters, temperature and top_p control randomness — low temp for deterministic checkout replies, maybe 0.0-0.3. max_tokens capped to reduce tail cost. also set stop sequences for structured responses.
02:05 Jon: on retries — we need patterns for network hiccups and 5xx, what's Redwood's recommendation?
02:12 Marcus: good question. we recommend two-phase approach: client-side idempotency + exponential backoff with jitter. if you can, include a request_id header so server can dedupe. for streaming, we typically do short reconnects (retry after small backoff and use resume tokens when possible), but if the session is stateful with server side caches, you might prefer to fall back to a sync regeneration.
02:45 Priya: resume tokens? can you show that?
02:48 Aditi: sure — when using the streaming websocket we emit a sequence_id in each chunk; on reconnect the client can request starting after last-seen sequence_id. it's not perfect for every SDK, but we have examples in the SDK repo.
03:05 Evan: our infra uses CDN+edge proxies; how do we handle connection drops long tail from user's poor mobile?
03:12 Marcus: two patterns: 1) keep a short timeout at the edge and let the client re-establish using resume tokens; 2) for very flaky networks we suggest server-side lightweight cache so a resumed request is quick. Redwood's dedicated mode gives more control over those caches, but hosted can be tuned too.
03:34 Lena: wanted to also highlight Optimize — it will recommend batching windows and quantization strategies based on your workload traces, which can cut per-token cost significantly.
03:45 Priya: is quantization production ready? does it change output quality?
03:49 Marcus: yes we onboard quantized variants per model; there's a quality delta that we measure in evals. Optimize provides suggestions with expected cost/latency delta and an eval set so you can see regressions. for a checkout assistant i'd lean conservative — 8-bit quant might be fine, 4-bit in some cases.
04:10 Evan: what's the model fallback story under load — we need graceful degradation during peaks.
04:15 Aditi: we support routing policies: primary model, then a cheaper compatible variant. console shows circuit-breaker metrics and automatic fallback when load or latency thresholds breach. you can also route by region or customer tier.
04:36 Priya: security: we need SOC2, SSO (SAML/SCIM), HSM/KMS for keys, and audit logs for PCI compliance checks.
04:45 Marcus: we are SOC2 and provide SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and KMS integrations — we can do customer-managed keys via cloud KMS or bring-your-own-HSM in Private deployments. i'll attach the security packet after the call.
04:58 Marta: great, could you also show the observability for a particular route — like token-level cost and p95 latencies?
05:05 Aditi: yes, in the Console here is a per-route dashboard, token breakdown, per-model cost, and tracing link that shows a waterfall of batching + kernel time + network time; sometimes transcription labels call kernels "kernal" or "kernel" inconsistently in exported notes, so ignore small name differences.
05:35 Evan: can we annotate certain prompts as sensitive so they never hit logs?
05:40 Marcus: yes, redaction rules and prompt filtering can be configured, and you can opt-out of fragment storage for specific routes.
05:50 Priya: pricing — we want hosted for quick time-to-prod but worried about unit cost at Black Friday volumes.
05:58 Lena: typical pattern is start hosted, measure, then reserve capacity for predictable peaks. we provide a tiered discount schedule and reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated. i'll send a comparison sheet.
06:10 Priya: ok good. show us a demo of a failing stream and a reconnect pattern end-to-end?
06:16 Aditi: sure — i'll simulate a socket drop. [screen action] so here's the log: connection open, tokens come in, then socket closes, client notices at 00:06:34 and does exponential backoff (200ms -> 500ms -> 1s); on reconnect the client requests resume from seq 42, server streams remaining tokens. if resume failed we fall back to re-issuing request with same request_id and dedupe on server.
07:10 Evan: what about idempotency for user actions like purchases — we can't risk duplicated charges if the assistant suggests something that triggers payment flows.
07:20 Marcus: keep LLM outputs deterministic for transactional flows (low temp), and enforce application-level idempotency tokens in your payment call. the LLM should only suggest actions; the payment system verifies token uniqueness.
07:35 Priya: any hard guarantees on p95 if we go hosted? our target was 300ms.
07:42 Aditi: hosted SLOs are published per model family; many customers observe p95 around 200–350ms for short prompts on infra-backed N models in our lowest-latency tier. Black Friday load will push you to reserved capacity for tighter SLOs.
07:58 Jon: do you instrument p50/p95 in trace? we need to ingest into our Datadog.
08:05 Aditi: yes we export traces via OpenTelemetry and can forward to Datadog; console also has native dashboards.
08:15 Marta: can Optimize proactively recommend batching windows given our traffic pattern?
08:20 Lena: yes — Optimize looks at sequence length distribution and concurrency and suggests batching target and cache TTLs, plus model variant recommendations.
08:30 Priya: ok this is helpful. what's a minimal POC look like?
08:35 Lena: two-week POC: 1) Redwood runs a bench with your sample prompts, measure p50/p95/cost, 2) enable streaming on a staging route with resume tokens and retry pattern, 3) Optimize run and a short findings doc. we can include a draft rollback plan.
08:55 Evan: timeline — we have an internal spike next Monday so two-week POC starting immediately would be ideal.
09:00 Lena: will propose start date tomorrow.
09:05 Priya: any limitations we should call out?
09:08 Marcus: streaming resume semantics depend on client library; some older mobile SDKs may not support resume tokens, in which case you either re-request or implement short-lived cache. also some model quant variants may have minor NLG regressions — Optimize flags them.
09:30 Marta: ok, last question — competitor LargeCloudAI says they have cheaper preemptible nodes. why Redwood?
09:36 Lena: main difference is production observability and unified API across hosted/dedicated/private plus first-class Optimize suggestions that close the loop between perf and cost. we also provide model fallback and circuit breakers out of the box.
09:55 Priya: perfect. can you recap next steps?
10:00 Lena: recap: Marcus will send security + KMS docs and a short note on redaction rules; Lena will share pricing and reserved capacity comparison; Marcus will prepare a benchmark script and run with Helios sample prompts; team to pick POC start date — propose 2026-05-24.
10:25 Evan: we'll confirm data and sample prompts by Friday.
10:35 Lena: thanks everyone, invite with POC kickoff to follow.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker attributions may be off, and there are a few misheard technical terms (e.g., CV cache for KV cache, kernal for kernel).

End of transcript.
